# NOTES: "The Young Naval Captain; or The War of All Nations" by Captain Ralph Bonehill (Edward Stratemeyer), Thompson & Thomas, Chicago, copyright 1902. Single book, no BOOK divisions.

## Front matter
- Title page: author Captain Ralph Bonehill; earlier works listed: "With Taylor on the Rio Grande," "Boys of the Fort," "The Tour of the Zero Club."
- Contents: Ch. I–XXX (titles below).
- Preface (signed Captain Ralph Bonehill): imaginary tale of a future war of all nations. Aims: (1) science advancing (electric lights, telephone, telegraph, wireless, navigable balloons, railroads once "impossible"); (2) US growth from 13 states to many more; flag from coast of Maine to coast of Luzon, Alaska to Texas and Porto Rico. Urges boys to seize opportunity; "humble rail-splitter or canal-boat boy can become President."

## Chapter list
I The United States Against the World; II First Battle on the Ocean; III An Interview with the Secretary of the Navy; IV Blowing Up of the Tien-Tsin; V Prisoners of the Sea; VI Out of a Living Tomb; VII An Attack on the Japanese Troops; VIII The Act of a Madman; IX Another Blowing Up; X The Fraudulent Message; XI An Urgent Call for the Holland XI; XII Defeat Turned Into Victory; XIII The Central American Canal; XIV Cast Upon the Shore; XV Tidal Waves and Whales; XVI Saving the Merchantman; XVII Playing the Spy; XVIII The Capture of Hang Chang; XIX News of the President's Daughter; XX The Cave Under the Ocean; XXI Out of One Danger Into Another; XXII A Run Not Wanted; XXIII The Fight off Cape Nome; XXIV Sinking of the Ivan II; XXV In Which the Holland XI is Captured; XXVI Prisoners on the Holland XI; XXVII The Defeat of the Enemy; XXVIII An Underwater Earthquake; XXIX The Rescue of Jean Fevre; XXX The Last Battle--Conclusion.

## Ch. I (1936, spring; "War is declared!" news by telephone from Washington cabinet chamber)
- Andy Greggs (18, blue eyes, curly brown hair, machinist, Standard Shipyard, Bridgeport) and Oscar Pelham (nearly 20, piercing black eyes, curly black hair) discuss: three new warships must be finished in six weeks by July 1; bonus $50,000.
- Oscar: "war against the world." Causes: US took Porto Rico, Philippines; Cuba became state; Canada broke from England; Yellow War of 1925 (China carve-up); South Africa/Boers freed; Turkey debt, US turned Turkish kingdom inside out in 1928.
- US: all North America (Panama Isthmus to Hudson Bay), West Indies, Hawaii, Philippines, others; corner of China and Japan. 100+ million people. President Jefferson McKinley Adams (6 yrs in office). Army 500,000; navy 500 warships.
- Commodore David Pelham (Oscar's father; Civil and Spanish-American war veteran, died; wife died earlier) ran Standard Ship Yard. Oscar studied at Edison's Electrical University, Llewellyn Park. Admired Holland X. at Elizabethport.
- Vermont inventor's submarine sank and blew up; Oscar predicted "sink fast enough, but won't come up." George Dross = oldest engineer.
- Oscar's boat design: aluminum and steel; 115 ft long, 16 wide, 8–11.5 ft high; cigar-shaped; windows; two electric screws; 23 knots. Named Holland XI.
- Midnight trial in Long Island Sound with Andy; success.

## Ch. II (war begins)
- Other nations want to cut US down. Cuba, Philippines admitted as states; Brazil, Chile, Peru, Honduras want entry; Mexico admitted via Texas. Aguinaldo dead; monument in Manila.
- New York war march; Empire building 56 stories; balloons.
- Navy: Holland I (1900) blown up by Italian engineer Gabretti (naturalized citizen, bribed $100,000); crew killed. $50,000 reward for Gabretti.
- Forts at Sandy Hook and Long Island: Hotchkiss bomb guns. Holland III, V, VI, IX, X listed; II, IV, VII, VIII destroyed/condemned.
- Foreign fleet off Nova Scotia; 15+ vessels; US sent 12 incl. armored cruiser Columbia (18,000 tons). Battle 20 miles off Sandy Hook on rainy Saturday: 13 foreign vs 12 US. Chicago sunk; German submarine (unnamed) wrecked three US cruisers; French sub failed (Indiana fired on it). US forced back to NY Harbor.

## Ch. III (Oscar to Washington)
- Letter from Andy: Oscar goes to Washington; Andy stays with model in storeroom at boarding house.
- Congressional Limited train. Senator Forbish (New York) gives letter of introduction.
- Secretary of the Navy: Short. Clerk. Oscar sees Short at 3:30 p.m. Model of Holland X. in office.
- Oscar: "give you the opportunity to destroy some of the foreign warships."

## Ch. IV (test; Tien-Tsin)
- Test at government experiment station pond at 5 p.m.; President Adams present. Model works; wireless... Model placed torpedo under warship model.
- Cost $200,000; or $500,000 for one month build (Navy accepted by telephone at 10 a.m.). Oscar worked 30 days. New Holland slid into New York bay on 29th day.
- Crew of ten: Oscar captain; Andy first lieutenant; George Dross head engineer.
- Cuban battle: Italian cruiser sunk by gunboat Yankee Doodle; US lost four old types.
- Commodore Garrison (Cuban waters): Chinese armored cruiser Tien-Tsin (from Brazil) bombarding Baracoa; 3,000 Celestials to land. Holland torpedoed Tien-Tsin with clock fuse set at 5 minutes; cruiser annihilated.
- French cruiser (Republique) fired dynamite shell at Holland.

## Ch. V (Prisoners of the Sea)
- Oscar touched keyboard; Holland jumped 2 ft; shell missed.
- Oscar pursued Republique underwater to within 50 yards; US gunboats in hidden Cuban bay (three old ships with dynamite guns) hit Republique 5 ten-inch shells; magazine exploded; cruiser sank onto Holland, burying it in sand; cruiser fore and aft on two hills. Torpedo fuse failed to go off.
- Air reservoir: 215 ft; enough for two hours (Marney the air man).

## Ch. VI (Living tomb)
- Oscar donned diver suit, exited through torpedo hole; keel of cruiser held Holland. Magazine explosion knocks him out. Holland gone; Oscar climbs out, arrives Cuban shore 2 miles west of Baracoa; falls asleep; wakes to ~1,000 Japanese troops.

## Ch. VII (Japanese attack)
- Japanese: "Chan-cera-ree!"; Oscar taken prisoner, tied to tree at river mouth.
- Holland surfaces (top-center plate); Andy with spy-glass; Andy frees Oscar with knife; Andy shoots soldier ("Hi-cha-kling!"). Both swim to Holland.
- Oscar orders dynamite bombs; two bombs kill ~50, wound many; another bomb kills Japanese commander. Japanese flee. Japanese goal: Havana, then Florida invasion.
- England sending 100,000+ men to attack Canada.

## Ch. VIII (Act of a Madman)
- Commodore Garrison's flagship; Garrison: Japanese won't reach Havana; orders Holland to Canada to meet American squadron off Canadian coast; British, French, German squadron escorting ~100,000 troops.
- Sargasso Sea entangles Holland 56 miles from land; bomb frees it.
- Gulf of St. Lawrence: Admiral Fielding. Lieutenant Raxtell (pale-faced, from flagship) assigned to watch Holland.
- Raxtell found in magazine room, about to fire dynamite bombs. (Illustration: "He was in the act of firing the explosive.")

## Ch. IX (Another Blowing Up)
- Oscar tackles Raxtell (madman: "We will all go to heaven!"; wanted shore leave denied). Walton (ammunition man) helps; Raxtell bound, leather mask. Raxtell put ashore at Boston later.
- Enemy fleet: 34 warships, 66 transports in semicircle.
- Torpedoes set: German gunboat Wilhelm II. (half hour), British cruiser Terrible (center, 20 min), French ship-of-the-line Philippe (10 min). All destroyed at 11:30. Philippe: only cabin boy survived. Terrible sank in two minutes; 200+ survived.
- Torpedo costs $8,600. Oscar requests highite bombs (new explosive; sends hundreds of small shells in circle).

## Ch. X (Fraudulent Message)
- Holland at Cape Cod harbor (Provincetown). Andy: President Adams' daughter Martha Adams kidnapped from White House (President at Cabinet meeting, Mrs. Adams at benefit meeting). Two servants drugged, one stabbed. Reward $100,000. Coach to Potomac; boat down river.
- Oscar admits he's sweet on Martha (met three times at shipyard).
- Fraudulent order sends Holland to a copper netting funnel trap with mine; Holland backs out. Messenger was English despatch boat officer (lieutenant). Despatch boat rammed; sank.

## Ch. XI (Urgent call)
- Commodore recommends Oscar's secret-marking idea for real messages; three false messengers hanged as spies.
- Anchor from fishing smack wrecks Holland's screw; repaired at Charlestown Navy Yard.
- Admiral Fielding's squadron of 26 cruisers and gunboats + 2 torpedo-boat destroyers. Battle near Casco Bay (Portland, Maine). US ships: Vermont, Canada, Oregon, Brooklyn, New Jersey, New York, Tennessee, Utah (blew up). German Berlin sunk; Italian gunboat Carlos II; French frigate Siene. Windsor (British) sunk by New Jersey.
- Oscar message: "Have just finished repairs and am at your service. OSCAR PELHAM, Captain, commanding Holland XI." Fielding: "Come to Casco Bay instantly."

## Ch. XII (Defeat turned into victory)
- Holland torpedoes British armored cruiser (attacking Iowa III); Coronet (French, dynamite guns) holed; two German cruisers vs. Virginia gunboat: torpedo between them. Two highite bombs on four-US-ship group; Turkish man-o-war and Italian corvette torpedoed; transport with 2,000 soldiers swept clear.
- President Adams sends thanks. Holland repaired at Boston.
- Fleet of fifty Chinese, Japanese, Russian warships toward Golden Gate.
- Admiral Alvin Chester (Pacific Squadron, knew Commodore David Pelham): message "You are wanted immediately on the pacific coast. If you do not come we are doomed. Chester."
- Route via Central American Canal (US built, $36 million).

## Ch. XIII (Central American Canal)
- Caribbean; Ambrose, Spanish settlement, despatches: "Be on your guard, or the Holland XI. will suffer..."
- Spaniards Carlos and others: "Pargloss ees vide awake." Nathan Pargloss (ex-Treasury, fired, $5,000/yr; sold secrets) plans to blow up canal locks. Oscar sets trap; Pargloss struggles, shot in shoulder, dives, drowns clinging to tree stump. Accomplice captured.

## Ch. XIV (Cast upon the shore)
- San Francisco: ovation. Honolulu: capital of Hawaii, 300,000 people. Enemy took islands; Diamond Head; Russians prevented massacre. Eight enemy warships in harbor; Oscar sets electric-wire-triggered bombs; Chinese commanders' food demand; they go ashore; prisoners in old fort. Foreign ships destroyed at 7:50 a.m.
- Underwater earthquake tidal wave (15 ft) casts Holland 200+ ft onto beach.
- Foreign warships Chinese, Japanese, Russian appear.

## Ch. XV (Tidal waves and whales)
- Andy and Oscar fire highite bomb on Russian ship; Japanese and Chinese fire on Holland. Tidal wave again; ships wrecked on rocks. Holland returned to Honolulu.
- Thirty-two foreign ships headed for SF.
- School of whales; one whale head-first into trap-door. Trap-door companionway; whale fitted.

## Ch. XVI (Saving the merchantman)
- Oscar shells whale's head with signaling shell; body falls.
- Thunderstorm; sailor dies (first death on Holland).
- American merchantman (bound Philippines) chased by two Japanese warships; Holland torpedoes first; second flees. Merchantman cheers.
- Oscar learns ~30 foreign ships near Golden Gate. Spies on conference on British ship Corcoran (captain Gresson). Oscar kills negro servant with knife.

## Ch. XVII (Playing the spy)
- Oscar poses as "Barton Peeks" (notorious British spy captured in St. Louis). Captain Gresson: attack on SF at sunrise; seven ships to attack; remainder to Alaskan coast under Russian admiral. Hang Chang (Chinese captain) and second Chinese captain (Chan Lee mentioned) plot using Martha Adams as hostage, demand a slice of California for new Chinatown.
- Oscar notes Holland gone (submerged); Hang Chang comes aboard. Secret code: "Sixteen, nine" = enemy here, go down.

## Ch. XVIII (Capture of Hang Chang)
- Hang Chang chained; Oscar knocks him down; Andy strikes him; Corcoran fires at Holland; Holland escapes.
- SF: admiral (naval commander) orders fleet to Alaska; Holland to accompany. Navy to build three more submarine craft; Oscar could be commodore.

## Ch. XIX (President's daughter news)
- Hang Chang reveals Martha on Chinese warship Green Dragon, sailed from Chesapeake to Cuba coast, alone. Oscar threatens torture (red-hot foot plates, branding iron); Hang Chang says Pekin and Shanghai are the ships here (Oscar: she's not on them).
- Hang Chang was on the Pekin (Chinese cruiser, sister of Tien-Tsin).

## Ch. XX (Cave under the ocean)
- Attack on SF/Oakland by Chinese Pekin (destroyed by fort guns) and Japanese; Oscar torpedoes Japanese ships (Tokio). Tokio's anchor chain tangled Holland's screw; Holland towed, freed by Oscar and Andy in diving suits; torpedo sinks Tokio.
- Cape Nome: 50,000 people; bank gold $35M, silver $18M.
- Holland trapped in sea-cave by landslide.

## Ch. XXI (Out of one danger)
- Sea serpent (30 ft, yellow eyes, green-white) hypnotizes Andy and Oscar; Oscar throws dynamite shell into its head; monster dies. Marney ("air man"), Walton (ammunition room), Gilson (general helper). Dross goes out with rifle and dynamite, blasts rock; escape.
- Lightning strikes Holland; George Dross unconscious; Andy shocked.

## Ch. XXII (A run not wanted)
- Oscar overwhelmed; Gilson helps; switchboard burnt out; Oscar turns steering; Holland runs in circle.

## Ch. XXIII (Fight off Cape Nome)
- Dross recovers; Oscar and Dross stop machinery. Duplicate switchboard installed.
- Russian cruiser Ivan II (largest in Russian navy; 100+ guns; 2,000 men) with 8 other ships approach; Russian captain orders bomb; Oscar catches it, fuse goes inside; he flings it up; both hurt (Andy's cheek skin taken, Oscar's left hand bruised).

## Ch. XXIV (Sinking of the Ivan II)
- Russian anti-submarine wires with alarm bell; Oscar's torpedo on a line drifts under Ivan II; sinks. 209 Russians captured at Cape Nome, including an admiral.
- Hang Chang attacks Oscar on deck; both go overboard.

## Ch. XXV (Holland XI captured)
- Andy kills Hang Chang with knife (four blows) and saves Oscar. Congress medal for bravery; Oscar to be commodore.
- Holland repairs near equator. Spanish cutter with ten men under Captain Roquez (Spanish); Walton overpowered by pitch plaster; Andy and Oscar bound; Marney killed by Roquez.
- Gabretti (Italian) revealed as engineer; plans to force Dross.

## Ch. XXVI (Prisoners on the Holland XI)
- Oscar frees himself by sawing strap on couch edge; frees Andy.
- Roquez, Gabretti; Canelli (Spanish sailor) guards.
- Roquez: "Americanos" defeated Spain in 1898.

## Ch. XXVII (Defeat of the enemy)
- Oscar and Andy overpower Roquez and Canelli; Oscar shoots Canelli with electric rifle. Roquez gagged in pantry.
- Gabretti kicked Dross; Oscar knocks Gabretti out. Ammunition men recovered. Enemy handed to garrison at Santiago de Cuba. Gabretti reward $50,000 to Oscar.

## Ch. XXVIII (Underwater earthquake)
- Foreign nations weary (16 naval battles, 4 won; 22 land contests, 3 won). US: army invades England (40,000, took two forts and a city); Japan; Philippines to China; Boers, Cape Colony, four South American republics join US.
- Caribbean heat 118°F; sink to bottom; volcano erupts; earthquake. Mention Martinique's St. Pierre (30,000 dead), Gromley Island (Prof. Gromley), NY quake with Battery shift.

## Ch. XXIX (Rescue of Jean Fevre)
- Holland escapes upheaval; reaches Santiago. Venezuela north coast quake.
- Wreck of French ship-of-the-line Bordeaux; sole survivor Jean Fevre (French dude who knew Martha; can't swim); rescued.

## Ch. XXX (Last battle--Conclusion)
- Fevre: Green Dragon hides in bay on Cuban coast, ten miles away.
- Oscar sees Martha on deck; Chinese admiral pursues her to bowsprit; she leaps; he shoots admiral. Oscar dives and rescues Martha; shot in shoulder; Andy hauls them aboard. Holland backs away; Andy torpedoes Green Dragon.
- Chesapeake: war over; foreign nations surrender. Martha found; reunion at Potomac with President and Mrs. Adams. President: Oscar commodore of new submarine fleet.
- Two years later: twelve submarines built; Andy commodore of one squadron; George Dross commodore of the other. Oscar becomes Rear Admiral Pelham; wife Martha. Ends "THE END."
